protocol: Exact vendor return 0x17224 for kill(1,SIGTERM) -> notify_rc("restart_wireless") -> verified existing notify shim -> native broker SIGUSR1 -> mock manager. No PID1 SIGTERM forwarded.
budget: Root-owned 0700 /run/leon-asus-wifi-recovery, O_EXCL root0600 once file with boot UUID. Consumed before enqueue; survives daemon and broker restarts; ambiguous failure never retries.
fixture_scope: Real production native broker and dual-ABI notify libraries, ARMEL same bridge sources with distinct synthetic ET_EXEC hash/return constants. Actual production launcher executes only rejection against synthetic executable. No actual ASUS monitor/rc/NVRAM/BSP/WiFi code runs.
limits: No Broadcom device, actual WiFi recovery or all-port continuity proven.
Existing ASUS restart_wireless may restart wireless/AiMesh/networkmap/printer and selected firewall/VLAN branches; it is not radio-only.
Constructor validates original ELF and fixed callsite. A new vendor ELF/broker/notify hash requires explicit rebuild/review.
Other monitor signals delegate to existing notify compatibility shim, preserving its TLS SIGUSR1 routing. No global loader configuration or original vendor binary is changed.
Root-owned private namespace checks prevent accidental host invocation; this is not a sandbox against malicious root.
An enqueue failure still consumes this boot's automatic recovery allowance; manual explicit management and separate guardian policy are unaffected.
